investigation.title: Investigation map
investigation.summary: Start with a question about a decision, transaction, or gap in oversight. Follow the records to the people with documented roles and test what the evidence supports.
facts: What we know
Every claim needs its own source and status. A record can verify a payment, a date, or that someone made a statement.
Who can act
Public researchers can examine public records. Any official request, compulsory process, or release needs its own authorized decision-maker.
choices: investigation-question
Frame a bounded legislative question before collecting records.
review
Open shared evidence and legal review when the record is ready to assess.
clemency-example
Use a fictional payment to test the difference between a transaction, a claim of access, and an exchange.
trading-example
Use a fictional trade to test the link between a decision and an order.
contracting-example
Use a fictional procurement file to test whether an intermediary performed the work it billed for.

investigation-question.title: Define the question
investigation-question.summary: Name the action or gap that warrants review, the dates, and the legislative decision the inquiry could inform.
facts: Start here
What reporting rule, selection procedure, or conflict safeguard might have failed? Identify the best lawful alternative explanation.
Who can act
Committee counsel checks jurisdiction, scope, and legislative purpose before formal inquiry or compulsory collection.
choices: investigation-records
The question defines which records can answer it and keeps collection within scope.
authority
Check the committee's authority and approval rules before making an official request.

investigation-records.title: Find and preserve records
investigation-records.summary: Record the issuer, date, exact location, original format, and any limits on use. Preserve provenance and distinguish a statement in a record from the event it describes.
facts: What is missing
Identify the smallest record request that would close a material gap. Check whether a public source or voluntary response is sufficient.
Who can act
The designated custodian holds records under the office's rules. Counsel and the authorized committee decision-maker review any compulsory request or sharing.
choices: follow-money
Trace a transaction only when a record identifies an actual event, amount, date, or counterparty.

follow-money.title: Follow the money
follow-money.summary: Trace the source, intermediary, account or entity, recipient, and any subsequent transfer. Treat every connection as a separate claim.
facts: Per connection
Show the supporting record, date, amount, parties, contrary evidence, and VERIFIED, INFERRED, or UNKNOWN status.
Stop point
If the next transfer lacks support, mark the link Not established. Matching amounts, nearby dates, or a shared bank can suggest a check but cannot fill a gap.
choices: investigation-custodian
Ask what the bank can document, which records are held, and what authority any further request needs.
investigation-entities
Resolve legal names, ownership, and control before attributing a benefit.
clemency-source
Inspect a fictional transfer one link at a time, starting at its documented source.
decisions
Bring supported links, contrary records, and documented gaps to the authorized decision-makers.

investigation-custodian.title: Bank as record custodian
investigation-custodian.summary: A bank may hold account-opening, payment, and settlement records. Treat it as a record custodian unless separate evidence establishes another role.
facts: Already held
Inventory the lawfully available payment confirmation and any approved statement excerpt. Mark missing dates, fields, or custody events.
What is missing
A posting record may confirm the destination account. The purpose of the payment may require separate agreements, invoices, or testimony.
Who may ask
Counsel checks the authorized committee's powers, financial privacy, and scope before any request. The public map grants no access to bank data.
choices: authority
The governing rules and applicable privacy restrictions determine the authorized records route.

investigation-entities.title: Resolve entities and accounts
investigation-entities.summary: Match an entity through its legal name, jurisdiction, dates, and reliable records. Identify separately who holds an account, controls an entity, or receives an economic benefit.
facts: Competing explanation
Similar names, shared addresses, and routine registered-agent services can connect unrelated entities in a search result. Verify each link before relying on it.
choices: investigation-roles
A person enters the map when a document or corroborated account establishes a relevant role.

investigation-roles.title: Identify documented roles
investigation-roles.summary: Label people by their role in the records, such as custodian, intermediary, recipient, witness, or decision-maker.
facts: What is missing
Distinguish a signature from authority to decide, an account posting from economic benefit, and a witness account from corroborated fact.
choices: test-evidence
Compare each proposed finding with the supporting record, adverse evidence, and credible alternatives.
witnesses
Counsel evaluates the authority and safeguards for any witness approach.

test-evidence.title: Test the evidence
test-evidence.summary: Review the strongest contrary records and lawful explanations with a second reviewer. Narrow the finding to what the sources support.
facts: VERIFIED
The identified original record supports the stated fact at a specific location.
INFERRED
The records support a stated interpretation, with the reasoning and alternatives visible.
UNKNOWN
The record cannot establish the claim. Name the gap or the evidence that could resolve it.
links: Roadmap: build and challenge the record
choices: review
Record how the review resolved each contradiction and which questions remain open.
decisions
Present the independent review and counsel's handling decisions before seeking approval for action.

review.title: Evidence and legal review
review.summary: Bring source-backed findings to independent review and counsel. Separate collection, access, and release decisions for each record.
facts: Handling
Record the custodian, allowed users, handling restriction, independent source, and release status. Keep restricted originals in the authorized office's secure system.
Sharing
A shared map can show why an item is withheld. Counsel and the authorized office decide what may be released, to whom, and for what use.
choices: follow-money
The reviewed record determines which payments can be traced and which connections remain unestablished.
test-evidence
Independent review checks provenance, contrary evidence, and what each source can establish.
witnesses
Separate voluntary contact, statutory immunity, and clemency before choosing a lawful witness mechanism.
coordination
Early coordination can establish authorized contacts. Any referral still needs state-law jurisdiction and a separate disclosure decision.
decisions
The approved evidentiary record is the basis for separate legislative and state-referral decisions.
authority
Verify which institution owns the decision and which approvals apply.

clemency-example.title: Did a fee buy clemency access?
clemency-example.summary: An applicant's business paid a consultant before a favorable clemency decision. What did the consultant deliver, and is there evidence of access or an exchange?
facts: Question
Compare the payment, the consultant's representations, the official timeline, and the services delivered before judging their relationship.
choices: clemency-source
Start with the original payment record and follow each documented link separately.
clemency-access
Review the consultant's documented representation as a separate question from the money trail.

clemency-source.title: Source: applicant's business
clemency-source.summary: The business's authorized statement excerpt shows a USD 12,000 debit on April 10, 2026.
facts: VERIFIED · Original record
Fictional bank statement A-01, April 10, line 8. The debit matches a USD 12,000 transfer confirmation.
Counterevidence
The confirmation references a consulting invoice. The payment alone establishes neither the actual service nor its purpose.
choices: clemency-intermediary
April 10, 2026 · USD 12,000 · VERIFIED. Fictional transfer confirmation A-02 names the consultant as payee. Invoice A-03 describes records preparation, which remains to be tested.

clemency-intermediary: April 10, 2026. Sender: applicant. Payee: consulting firm. USD 12,000. Payment reference C-0410. Status: posted.
Invoice A-03 describes records preparation. The transfer record cannot identify the purpose of the payment or establish access to a decision-maker.

clemency-intermediary.title: Intermediary: consulting firm
clemency-intermediary.summary: The consultant's receipt names the firm's operating account. Its invoice describes a records review and application preparation.
facts: VERIFIED · Original record
Fictional invoice A-03, April 8, item 1, and receipt A-04, April 10, line 2. These establish what was billed and acknowledged.
Counterevidence
A later sales message describes possible access. The billing documents and the sales claim have different evidentiary uses.
choices: clemency-account
April 10, 2026 · USD 12,000 · VERIFIED. The fictional authorized deposit excerpt A-05 matches the receipt by payment reference. The deposit alone does not establish anyone's purpose.

clemency-account: April 10, 2026. Account holder: consulting firm. Credit USD 12,000. Reference C-0410. Credit line 5.
The consulting firm's receipt matches the payment reference. Other credits appear in the same account. Later payments need their own evidence.

clemency-account.title: Account: firm operating funds
clemency-account.summary: An authorized bank excerpt shows the deposit into the firm's operating account. Other receipts in the same account complicate attribution of later payments.
facts: VERIFIED · Original record
Fictional bank excerpt A-05, April 10, credit line 5. The account holder name matches the consulting firm's receipt.
UNKNOWN · Gap
The common account balance cannot identify which incoming funds paid a later invoice.
choices: clemency-recipient
April 14, 2026 · USD 3,500 · VERIFIED outgoing payment from the firm's account in A-06. Attribution of that payment to the applicant's deposit is UNKNOWN because funds were pooled.

clemency-recipient: April 14, 2026. Sender: consulting firm operating account. Payee: records specialist. USD 3,500. Reference: specialist invoice A-07.
The dated delivery receipt corroborates the specialist's work. Account balances do not establish which incoming funds paid this invoice.

clemency-recipient.title: Recipient: records specialist
clemency-recipient.summary: A USD 3,500 payment went to a specialist that supplied records research. This establishes the account recipient and supports an ordinary-services explanation.
facts: VERIFIED · Original record
Fictional wire A-06, April 14, and provider invoice A-07, April 13, identify the payee and USD 3,500 amount.
Counterevidence
A dated delivery receipt and completed work product corroborate the services. The file contains no subsequent transfer record from the specialist.
choices: clemency-transfer-gap
Subsequent transfer · UNKNOWN date, amount, and recipient. The available records end at the specialist. No transfer to a decision-maker is established.

clemency-transfer-gap: Fictional record A-06 establishes only the consulting firm's payment to the specialist on April 14, 2026.
There is no supporting record for a subsequent transfer. Its date, amount and recipient remain unknown.

clemency-transfer-gap.title: Subsequent transfer: not established
clemency-transfer-gap.summary: The available records end at the specialist. There is no supported connection from the specialist to an official or decision-maker.
facts: UNKNOWN · Stop here
No authenticated transfer, date, amount, or recipient is available for a further step. The ledger stops here unless lawfully obtained new records establish a link.
choices: clemency-access
A separate authenticated message can be tested as a claim of influence. It supplies no missing transaction record.

clemency-access.title: Test the claim of access
clemency-access.summary: The consultant wrote that they could get the applicant's file in front of a decision-maker. The message verifies the statement and leaves actual access unknown.
facts: VERIFIED · Original record
Fictional email A-08, April 15, body paragraph 2, contains the representation.
Counterevidence
Routine submission instructions in A-09 offer a lawful route for the file. No meeting log or corroborated witness places the consultant with the decision-maker.
choices: clemency-decision
Compare the recorded decision date to the separate payment and access records. The timing alone cannot establish a causal link.

clemency-decision.title: A decision follows
clemency-decision.summary: A fictional public decision register records approval on May 18, 2026. The sequence warrants checking the review process and any communications.
facts: VERIFIED · Original record
Fictional decision register A-10, May 18, entry 14. It records the outcome and date.
Counterevidence
A March 28 receipt shows the application was in the ordinary review queue before the consulting payment. The reason for the decision is UNKNOWN.
choices: clemency-test
Test communications, agreements, services performed, and routine review before describing any exchange.

clemency-test.title: Challenge the exchange theory
clemency-test.summary: Compare the consultant's agreement and work product with submission logs and authorized communications. Seek contrary evidence and independent corroboration.
facts: INFERRED · Ordinary services
The agreement, records delivery and separate invoice support a legitimate services explanation. Actual access, an exchange, and a transfer to any official remain UNKNOWN.
choices: clemency-finding
The second reviewer and counsel separate documented payments from unsupported claims and decide whether any release or next step is authorized.

clemency-finding.title: Finding: a narrower record
clemency-finding.summary: The record establishes payment and completed services. It is insufficient to establish purchased access, an exchange, or a transfer to an official.
facts: Congressional option
Consider a disclosure-policy review if the verified records expose a systemic gap.
State referral
No applicable state-law basis or competent recipient is established on these facts. Record a hold decision.
choices: review
Preserve the narrower finding and the unresolved claims for independent review and correction.

trading-example.title: Did a nonpublic decision inform a trade?
trading-example.summary: A fund bought shares before an agency announcement. Who knew what and when, and when was the order decided?
choices: trading-records
Reconcile order entry and execution times with disclosure times and the information actually available to the trader.

trading-records.title: Compare order and disclosure records
trading-records.summary: Fictional confirmation B-01 shows a USD 48,000 buy at 10:13 UTC on June 9, 2026. Agency bulletin B-02 was public at 14:00 UTC that day.
facts: VERIFIED
The trade and publication timestamps are in separate original records.
Counterevidence
Fictional broker instruction B-03 was logged June 3. Its conditions match an automated execution triggered by a publicly available price.
choices: trading-finding
Check whether the existing order could have been changed and whether any reliable record connects the trader to nonpublic information.

trading-finding.title: Finding: ordinary execution is supported
trading-finding.summary: An independently timestamped broker audit supports execution under a pre-existing instruction. The record supplies no evidence that the trader received or acted on nonpublic information.
facts: Disposition
The evidence supports a lawful explanation. Close the lead on this record and retain the audit trail for correction if new evidence appears.
choices: review
Record the competing explanation and why it fits the independently verified records.

contracting-example.title: What did a contract intermediary deliver?
contracting-example.summary: An agency paid a contractor that used an intermediary. Can the agency verify services, prices, and the award decision?
choices: contracting-records
Compare the award file, invoice, delivery, and agency acceptance before judging the arrangement.

contracting-records.title: Compare award, invoice, and delivery
contracting-records.summary: Fictional award C-01 allows subcontracting. Agency payment C-02 shows USD 80,000 on July 17, 2026. Deliverables and invoices support most of the payment.
facts: VERIFIED
Payment C-02, entry 4, and acceptance record C-03 identify the award and dates. A USD 8,000 milestone line lacks a dated approval in the supplied file.
Counterevidence
A system-migration log identifies a plausible missing-record explanation. Other dated work products support performance under the contract.
choices: contracting-finding
Check the original approval record and payment terms. Keep any finding within the documented exception if the missing item cannot be recovered.

contracting-finding.title: Finding: a documentation gap
contracting-finding.summary: The file does not verify milestone approval before payment. Subcontracting itself was permitted. The missing record cannot establish fraud, an improper award, or who caused the gap.
facts: Next decision
An authorized committee may ask about record retention or consider reporting changes. Track any correction when the original file is found.
State referral
The evidence establishes no separate state-law basis on the current record.
choices: congressional-action
A supported records-control gap can inform authorized legislative follow-up without any referral.
